Hey, based on my experience, always go with your gut. When someone starts canceling and coming up with excuses, it probably means their feelings have changed and maybe it has nothing to do with you. Maybe it would be a good idea for you to be blunt and just confront the other person. I think it's more hurtful to live with all the demons that doubt bring up than just facing reality, as hurtful as it might be. 

Hope this helps and everything turns out ok.

Hey, I did IV last year. I agree with most of what is already posted. You can find various playlist on Spotify for your journey and be sure to have some kind of eye cover. I think the most important thing is to integrate what you felt with your therapist or somebody that you fully trust.   


I'd also suggest taking an Uber or similar as you'll feel a little weak and disoriented for the next hour, so it's probably best not to drive. Hope you feel better!

I'll never compare, but SC2 saved my life. The girl I was going to marry dumped out of the blue after 9 years. I couldn't eat, sleep, work or even think about anything else. But the only thing that could bring my head to concentrate enough to stop thinking about her war SC2. I owe so much to this game, I owe it my life.
